KONGMOON INCIDENT.

label: text
text: Owners

label: text
text: The facts, as disclosed in evidence, were "that the ship (the Leung Kwong) was ordered from Hongkong to Kongmoon by her owners on July 9. On arrival there everything was apparently quiet, but the crew deserted. The master asked a British ship in port to stand by, but the reply came back regretting inability so to do and the ship in question left for Hongkong.

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: As master, you were monarch of all you surveyed?

label: text
text: Mr. James R. Wilson, the master of a Chinese owned'ship, owing to representations as to the lives of himself and subordinate officers being endangered and to there being no food aboard, left his ship at Kongmoon and together with his officers returned to Hongkong. This morning he was the plaintiff in a case in the Summary Court. He sued his owners, the Cheat Wo Steamship Company, for $1,000 (salary and value of personal property loss).

label: text
text: Cross-examined by Mr. D. McCallum, who represented the owners, Mr. Wilson said that he engaged European officers and received $700 a month with which to pay them.

label: text
text: Mr. Wilson flew his distress signal but, in spite of there being a British gunboat in the harbour, no response was forthcoming. Shortly after the purser came aboard and told the master that his life was in danger and that he had better leave the ship. As there was no food aboard and no crew, the master took his papers and ship's ammunition to the Customs House and returned with his officers to Hongkong.

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: Do you suggest that the purser who came aboard and told you your life was in danger was the agent of the Company?

label: text
text:
Witness: Yes, he took the place of the compradore on that trip.
Mr. McCallum: Are you in the habit of taking orders from the compradore?

label: text
text:
Mr. McCallum: So far as discipline is concerned?
Witness: No.

label: paragraph_title
text: IN ENEMY WATERS.

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: So far as the ship is concerned, did you consider she was captured?

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: When you got to Kongmoon did you consider you were in enemy's waters? Witness: Yes.

label: text
text: Witness: No, I know the ship was all right as she was Chinese-owned. But our lives were not safe.

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: Did you desert her?

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: Were your orders to take her to Kongmoon and leave her there?

label: text
text: Witness: No, I was obliged to leave.

label: text
text: Witness: If they had been we should never have gone.

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: Were you informed by the purser that your lives were in danger?

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: He told you purely as a friendly act.

label: text
text: Witness: No; he was in league with the owners to get our money stopped.

label: text
text: Mr. McCallum: He was nice to you?

label: text
text: Witness: Yes, a man who wants to do himself a good turn is usually very nice.

label: text
text: The evidence of the master having been corroborated by Mr. Thomas Aberdeen Nicholas, the Chief Officer, Mr. McCallum addressed the Court, contending that the purser could never have been the agent for the company and in a position to discharge a ship's master in circumstances such as these. Once a ship had been deserted in this way she became a total loss and the master made himself liable to an action by the Company.

label: text
text: Discussion here ensued between counsel (Mr. G. R. Haywood being for the plaintiff) and it was pointed out to Mr. McCallum that Sections 157 and 158 of the Merchant Shipping Act could not be made to apply in the case of a master.

According to enquiries made at the Club this morning the story as it had reached there was that six bar boys had been stopped in a junk when two hours journey from Macao and had been ill-treated and detained.

label: text
text: The largest locomotive ever made, shown here, was fast passed first tests, at Pittsburgh, where it was built by the Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company, with flying colours. Some idea of the tremendous size of the rail giant is given by comparison with the 300 men who were employed in constructing it. The locomotive is 152 feet long and is built in three sections so that it can take sharp curves safely. It weighs 1,275,800 pounds, or 0.37½ tons, generates 7,125 horsepower, and exerts a maximum pulling force of 277,500. Each of the driving wheels is more than five feet in diameter and the cabs are 16 feet high and more than 11 feet wide. When going down hill, ahead of long strings of coal cars, the locomotive will generate power and turn it back into the transmission line. It is the first of 30 ordered by the Virginian railway for its $15,000,000 electrification project between Mullens, W. and Roanoke.

Rumours that have circulated as to the departure from the Colony this week of His Excellency the Governor must have had as their origin the imminent departure of his A.D.C., Capt. R.A.R. Neville, R.M.T.I., who has booked passage Home by the Empress of Australia and leaves tomorrow.
He was last seen alive by the assistant superintendent of the Home at 10 o'clock on Monday night, and he then appeared to be his usual self.

label: text
text: Captain Richardson had been staying at the Sailors' Home, Des Vœux Road West, since last Friday, and he was apparently waiting for a suitable opening as a ship's master, on one of the local vessels.

His presence here will be missed and the "China Mail" echoes the sentiments of all residents in wishing Capt. The discovery that something had occurred was made on Tuesday morning when a pool of blood met the gaze of an inmate who was passive a window of the room occupied by the Captain. A report was immediately made to Divisional Inspector Peter Grant, of No. 7 Police Station, who visited the Home with Sergeant Fender.

label: text
text: The police officers found the deceased lying on the floor in a pool of blood with two broken lemonade bottles beside him. The upper part of one of the bottles, which had broken with a sharp point, was found embedded in the right foot, and this had severed an artery. A sponge rag wound round the foot indicated that the deceased had made an unsuccessful attempt to stop the flow of blood by bandaging the wound. One of the heads of the lemonade bottles was found outside the window. It was clear that the deceased had attempted to open the lemonade bottles by striking the heads against the window sill and in doing so dropped a fragment on to his bare foot just above the slipper.

label: text
text: None of the inmates appears to have heard any cries for help from the deceased, and his accidental death was only discovered in the morning.

label: text
text: The body was removed to the public mortuary, and the arrangements for the funeral were made by the superintendent of the Sailors' Home.

label: text
text: The deceased is said to have been about 50 years old.

label: paragraph_title
text: MR. BIRD DRAWS A DISTINCTION.

label: paragraph_title
text: BUILDING LIABILITIES

label: text
text: The Supreme Court “building” case in which the award of the Hon. Mr. H. W. Bird as an arbitrator is questioned, drew to a close before Sir Henry Cowper Gollan yesterday, and judgment was reserved.

label: text
text:
Mr. Jenkin, for the plaintiff, who asks that the award should be set aside, said yesterday afternoon that his case was that Mr. Bird's award was made with every intention of doing justice as between man and man, but that in so doing he allowed himself to be carried away by the usual practice instead of abiding by the contract.
Mr. Bird: I may be wrong in law but I am quite sure my award was just.

label: text
text: The Hon. Mr. C. G. Alabaster, closing his case for the contractor in whose favour Mr. Bird had found, argued that it was no reason for upsetting an award to state that an arbitrator did not consider a point which was not taken. The arbitrator had made up his mind at the time of the arbitration but he had said that it was a mind open to consider any fresh arguments which might be raised.

label: text
text: In his final address to His Lordship, Mr. Jenkin said that it was impossible to say that there had been no miscarriage of justice when an arbitrator took his judicial seat and then said, "Now look here, this matter is decided and unless you have further light to shed upon it I shall decide against you."
